## TSFMC Standard Operating Procedure
The following document outlines the general procedures and behavior marines should expect to have. Failure to adhere to this document may result in warnings, docked pay, demerits, dismissal from service, or even execution, depending on how bad the transgression is or if multiple infractions occurred. Allowance will be made for honest mistakes, [italic]willful disobedience[/italic] and intentional harm towards fellow marines will be punished.
# [color=#526875]Trans-Solarion Federation (TSF)[/color] - Colossus Sector Mission Statement
We are [color=#990000][italic]not[/italic][/color] civilians, mercenaries for hire, or would-be murderers. We are Marines. We are soldiers. We are professionals. We live and die for our brothers-in-arms, our superiors, the government, and the loyal civilians of this sector. The TSFMC is the strongest military power in this sector, and we use that strength to destroy our enemies, but it is only as strong as every marine fighting for it. We treat our brothers-in-arms and outsiders with dignity and respect, not because we are afraid of their ire, but because it is right. Where cowards falter, we stand strong and unafraid, because we are the TSF Marine Corps.
#[color=#526875]TSFMC[/color] Standard Operating Procedure:
1. The Colonel is the ultimate authority in the Sector and has the ability to warn, assign demerits, demote, dismiss, or execute marines who are a [color=#526875]danger[/color] to the [color=#526875]TSFMC[/color], do not follow orders, or harm civilian life.
2. Communicate: lack of communication kills soldiers. Tell us where you are going, even if you are alone. Report in immediately with task and location when asked. Communicate with others when on task. If you are calling for help when you are in active combat, you are already dead.
3. Assist your fellow marines where possible: If you have no prior orders superceding a call for backup, then get out there as fast as possible.
[italic]3.a. Likewise, do not endanger your fellow marines by rushing into pointless battles you cannot win. Retreat, regroup, coordinate, re-engage with stronger numbers. Do not force someone to save you for the 20th time.[/italic]
4. Remain professional on comms: we are marines, not immature highschoolers. This includes TSF comms, Broadband, and the announcement console. Banter and discussion is acceptable, treating fellow marines and unaffiliated civilians like trash is not. Especially avoid berating your fellow marines on TSF comms, sewing discord and creating a toxic atmosphere.
5. Treat the civilian population with dignity and respect: we are here to protect them from the PDV and rogue elements, just as they are here to support the TSF as the rightful ruler of the sector.
6. When out in the field, whether guarding contraband vaults, patrolling the sector, or monitoring Halcyon, aim to hail first, even if it is an IFFless ship. Allow for at least 30 seconds, unless they choose to run or open fire. If they escape, consider it a win that they were too afraid to face you.
7. Avoid gibbing people where possible.
8. Do not fire on Medical Dispatch ships without a VERY good reason. Other medical ships may be included if they are actively rescuing and not being used for war efforts.
# With Regards to Civilians:
1. When hailing any civilian ship, allow anywhere from 1-5 minutes for response. Civilians are sometimes oblivious and may not notice right away. Be flexible: the civilian may be SSD, in critical condition, or the vessel may be abandoned. Investigate first, do not simply fire because you didn't receive a response.
[italic] 1.a. This does not include confirmed Chimera or otherwise captured ships that actively pose a threat to you or others.[/italic]
2. Do not arrest civilians for the possession of contraband: seize their contraband, fine them and let them go.
3. If the civilian chooses to flee or open fire, aim to disable and arrest over gibbing.
[bold]With Regards to IFFless:[/bold]
1. If it looks like a civilian ship, ask them to turn their IFF on. They are more likely hiding from PDV and pirates than from TSF.
2. If it looks like a PDV ship, you may choose to hail or immediately open fire, depending on the situation you find yourself in.
[bold]With Regards to Prisoners:[/bold] Treat them with dignity and respect. Do not perform experiments on them, do not leave them without basic clothes, PDA, food and water. Torture should be avoided unless absolutely necessary, i.e. to reveal critically important information.
[bold]The Chain of Command:[/bold]
The CoC is a tool to keep order and discipline in the [color=#526875]TSFMC[/color], but it is not a weapon to brutalize your fellow marines. Follow it, obey orders, and treat your fellow marines with respect, no matter if they are above you, the same rank as you, or below you.
The Colonel: The ultimate authority in the sector, the Colonel is responsible for overseeing the bigger picture, and deals with diplomacy and overall organization through the Captain and FTLs.
The Captain: The Colonel's second in command, they are reponsible for organizing the Colonel's overall goals and making sure the FTLs and marines are on task.
The FTLs: Fire Team Leaders are responsible for the day-to-day operations, particularly in combat and in training fellow marines. They will frequently be out on the field performing strikes against PDV forces and investigating situations.
Marines: The fighting force and backbone of the Marine Corps, your job is to find a superior officer for assignment and follow their orders. If FTLs are busy, then seeing if the specialists need help is a good way to apply your skills. If you are still having trouble getting assigned, then seek out the Colonel.
The Engineers/Corpsman: These two are not beneath marines, they are specialists who excel at their chosen field. Depending on their area of expertise, they may even be considered slightly above marines in the CoC, though officially they are equal.
[bold]- Colonel Talon Voss, Winter Solstice: Colossus Sector Oversight Detachment (CSOD)
As an OOC note Solider, SOP's are not enforcable by admins in any way, shape, or form. Colonels (or Captain if no Colonel present) can choose to VOID SOP at any time. This exists simply as a base for new players to learn how to play.
